q: I asked him about him parental leave. He said the county did not offer any, kind of chuckled saying “most of the country” doesn’t offer it.
c: County employee in Virginia, due in July, under a year in the job; HR on parental leave.

q: Not to mention he kept reminding me my job isn’t “protected” during that time and that I could come back in 5-6 weeks. Which, no honey, I’m not coming back in 6 weeks.
c: Same author.

q: She acted like she had no idea why I would call if I hadn’t been there for a full year. Then she had the HR guy I’ve been talking to and herself call me back, and he explained how I don’t qualify for short term disability because I have to be there for a year or FMLA
c: Same author calling a second HR contact about FMLA paperwork; earlier told she did qualify for disability.

q: He basically told me I could use whatever PTO I have etc. which isn’t much since everything is accrual. I have 80 hrs lol.
c: Same author.

q: I’m mad at this country for not giving a rats ass about pregnant woman and mothers. But expect me to work like a slave until I give birth.
c: Same author.

q: Doing ANYTHING feels so exhausting! All I did was sort and collect dirty laundry around the house and I literally had to lay down.
c: First-time mum at 30 weeks, trying to get the nursery ready.

q: we do have a cleaner who comes and deep cleans our home once a month and it is very worth it. If you are considering it, I would 1000% recommend it.
c: Same author replying to another pregnant woman mid-renovation.

q: That’s pretty much why I’m having mine done so I can try and avoid induction! I can’t see it being very pleasant but like you say it’s worth a go!
c: UK; consultant agreed to sweeps several times a week from 39 weeks before an induction at 41.

q: Scared I went to the hospital alone leaving my husband with our 1 year old.
c: Second-time mum two weeks after a fast birth; first trip to hospital in early labour.

q: We tried calling all of our friends to see who could stay with our son no one answered my husband ended up calling one of his military buddies who came in clutch and was at the house in 15 minutes.
c: Same author, after her waters broke at home at night; she gave birth in the hospital hallway.

q: I still have issues processing this birth story because I dont want to label it as traumatizing my husband says it was beautifully tragic and that hes proud of me.
c: Same author.

q: From my experience of talking with friends and family, a lot of money go into a baby shower and most family members don’t buy from the baby registry at all. Or a lot less people show up than originally RSVPed.
c: Very early in pregnancy, plans to skip the shower and registry and ask for a baby fund; crossposted to r/BabyBumps.

q: I also have a bad habit of having clutter everywhere, so the thought of a  bunch of gifts from everyone and taking forever to open/ discard boxes stressses me out even more. The economy is really bad too and i just don’t have the heart to put ourselves in debt
c: Same author; ends 'Be as brutally honest as possible.'

q: when I ranted to my husband he said “just be positive, you’re being negative”. That’s SO easy for other people to say when they’re not going through it!
c: First-time mum at 37+4, with swelling, reflux, nausea back and broken sleep.

q: Y’all weren’t lying when you said the third trimester is the hardest.
c: Same author.

q: I love my baby boy so much but I miss my body. I miss looking sexy.
c: Eight days postpartum after gaining 45 lbs.

q: I'm just so tired of being sick and unwell during this pregnancy. On paper everything has been perfect, but I definitely don't feel great.
c: Past 21 weeks; nausea eased, then an existing eye problem returned; specialists can't see her for a month.

q: FTM, of course I start to notice this today when both my PT and OB are out for the weekend already for me to ask.
c: Almost 29 weeks, feeling pelvic heaviness.

q: My husband had two weeks of paternity leave and his employers pat themselves on the back for that like it's even remotely enough.
c: Seven-week-old who won't settle; husband is the sole earner, gone almost 12 hours a day.

q: we spent almost a week in the hospital postpartum so he was only home with the baby for a week before going back.
c: Same author.

q: His mom is not maternal and is clearly uncomfortable around babies, holding her for a minute before making an excuse to leave like "I'll get out of your hair" when I'm actually desperate for help.
c: Same author; her own parents live far away.

q: I bought a one piece swimsuit at Target and my boobs looked massive and had no support. I bought the Hunza G scrunchy one piece and same deal.
c: 26 weeks, shopping for a babymoon swimsuit.

q: Not long after, my midwife said another midwife would be taking over because she hadn’t slept in over 24 hours and “her brain wasn’t working.” Hearing that while I was in labor was terrifying.
c: First-time mum in Canada, six days after an induction under a midwife team.

q: Her response was, “The hospital said you’re 5 cm?” almost annoyed, and then she said I’d have to wait because there’s a whole procedure for an epidural.
c: Same author on the phone to her midwife from the hospital.

q: Going forward, I honestly don’t think I could ever trust midwife care again after what happened. As a first-time mom, this experience has been incredibly scary.
c: Same author, considering a complaint and a birth debrief.
